chunks: They will say: 'All praise be to God Who has fulfilled the promise He had made to us, and bequeathed to us this land for dwelling in the garden wheresoever we like.' How excellent the recompense for those who act!

key_terms.أَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ: He bequeathed to us the Earth

ai.seo_question: What do the inhabitants of Paradise say to thank God for His promise?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Az-Zumar is often cited to illustrate the ultimate state of the faithful in Jannah, where they inherit the Earth not merely as a physical space but as a domain of divine proximity and eternal bliss. The phrase 'wherever we wish' (haythu nasha'u) is interpreted by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai to signify the expansion of their spiritual capacity and authority within the Garden, reflecting the culmination of their worldly worship. This declaration serves as the final reward for the 'workers' (al-'amilin), linking their earthly efforts directly to their eternal inheritance.
